cohorts.scope: One independent source-present cold cohort: eight frozen recipes, three balanced fresh workers each, exact logits/KV/positions/selections/RNG/output equality and zero observed swap growth. All recipes use the same 150+8 public bound. Complete worker RSS includes SDK, supervisor, dashboard, WAN relay and audit; the largest replicate qualifies the observed RAM budget. Coupled boundary beats the best eligible tested incumbents on all-link TCP streams and full request latency in Low and Medium, with slower online TTFT/decode and more RAM. Two additional boundary workers change the non-collusion contract; topology-specific SOTA rows remain separate. Checkpoint/tokenizer distribution, physical wire and Internet RTT are unmeasured. Original historical cohorts and preflight-rejected attempts supply no replicates. Full results: docs/research/private-boundary-tiers-reference.md.

cohorts.scope: Independent nine-client confirmation of maintained prepared, serial/u32 boundary and parallel/uniform-residue boundary execution at 150+8 tokens, three balanced replicates per recipe under shared native 100/40 caps. All 78,842,880 checked logit/KV values and complete state/output commitments agree with zero observed swap growth. Parallel/residue decode rises 52.87% versus serial/u32, with 2.13 MB fewer TCP-stream bytes and 1.48% lower request latency; client CPU is nearly unchanged and median RSS rises 2.61%. Largest candidate complete-worker peak is 224.13 MiB, within observed Low and Medium ceilings. Against maintained prepared execution, traffic falls 23.70% and request latency 24.18%, while decode remains 32.68% slower and online first-text delay rises 8.00%. SDK, supervisor, dashboard, relay and audit share the measured worker. Original sources and evidence are preserved; stronger read-only metric/build audits reproduce the original summary. The swap-rejected attempt and original screen supply no observations. Source/tokenizer delivery, physical wire and Internet RTT remain excluded; the additional boundary workers retain their distinct trust/topology contract. This confirms the selected finalists, not seven earlier incumbents or unmeasured longer outputs. Full costs and replay: docs/research/private-boundary-decode-followup.md.

cohorts.scope: Separate nine-client 150+32 long-output screen of the frozen maintained prepared, serial/u32 boundary and parallel/uniform-residue boundary finalists under shared native 100/40 caps. Every response reaches 32 outputs and 31 decode intervals; all 336,605,184 checked logit/KV values and complete state/output commitments agree with zero observed swap growth. Parallel/residue decode rises 53.79% versus serial/u32 and removes exactly 8,503,680 head-reply bytes. Against maintained prepared execution, TCP streams fall 16.84%, full request latency 20.83% and startup-through-cleanup time 15.51%, while decode remains 32.77% slower and online first text is 6.96% later. Largest candidate complete-worker peak is 230.69 MiB, within observed Low and Medium ceilings. All owners and costs retain the original SDK benchmark windows. This first longer-workload screen does not borrow confirmation status or observations from 150+8. Source/tokenizer delivery, physical wire and Internet RTT remain excluded; additional boundary workers retain their distinct trust/topology contract. Full costs and replay: docs/research/private-boundary-decode-followup.md.
